question.problem:
The vectors ${a}_{1},$ ${a}_{2},$ and ${a}_{3}$ are given below. Determine whether $B=\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}\}$ is a basis of $\text{Span}\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}\}.$ If that is the case, find ${x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{2},$ where ${a}_{3}={x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}.$

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}14 \\ 9\end{aligned}]
$$
question.worked_solution:
We want to determine if $B$ is indeed a basis of $\text{Span}\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}\}.$ So, we want to find ${x}_{1},{x}_{2}\in R$ such that 

$$
{x}_{1}{{[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{a}_{1}}+{x}_{2}{{[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{a}_{2}}={{[\begin{aligned}14 \\ 9\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{a}_{3}}.
$$

This equation is equivalent to the system

$$
\{\begin{aligned}2{x}_{1}-2{x}_{2}=14 \\ 2{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}=9\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we reduce the augmented matrix of the system to reduced row echelon form (RREF):

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,[\begin{aligned}2 & -2 & 14 \\ 2 & -1 & 9\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 7 \\ 2 & -1 & 9\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 7 \\ 0 & 1 & -5\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & -5\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

From the RREF matrix above, we see that the pivot columns are the $1$st and $2$nd columns. So,  $B$ is indeed a basis of $\text{Span}\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}\}.$
Also, the matrix tells us that ${x}_{1}=2$ and ${x}_{2}=-5,$ meaning that

$$
2\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{a}_{1}}+(-5)\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{a}_{2}}={{[\begin{aligned}14 \\ 9\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{a}_{3}}.
$$

Therefore, ${x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{2}=2\cdot (-5)=-10.$
